title: Reactor Code Checksum
story:
Every reactor code carries a checksum: the sum of its digits. The control panel won't accept a code until you confirm it.

Input: one whole number `N` (0 ≤ N ≤ 2000000000).

Output: the sum of the digits of N.

Example: `1234` prints `10`.
hints: The last digit of n is `n % 10`.
`n / 10` chops the last digit off. Repeat while `n > 0`.
Add `n % 10` to a running total, then `n = n / 10;`, inside `while (n > 0)`. For 0 the loop never runs and the total stays 0.
